results.title: Lumentum FY2026 Q4 Earnings Highlights: Revenue Doubled YoY to $1.01 Billion, Non-GAAP EPS Up 267%, Q1 Guidance Significantly Above Expectations
results.content:
Core View

Lumentum (LITE.US) reported results for the fiscal fourth quarter ended June 27, 2026. Net revenue rose approximately 109% year-over-year to $1.01 billion, modestly above market expectations. Non-GAAP adjusted EPS surged 267% year-over-year to $3.23, significantly beating estimates. Non-GAAP gross margin broke through 50% to reach 50.4%, while operating margin hit 36.6%, demonstrating stronger profit leverage than revenue growth. On a GAAP basis, the company recorded a net loss of approximately $7.2 billion due to a one-time non-cash debt extinguishment charge. Guidance for the next fiscal quarter (FY2027 Q1) shows revenue midpoint growth of about 135% year-over-year and roughly 8% above consensus, with non-GAAP operating margin guided near 40%, underscoring continued strong demand from AI optical communications. After-hours trading saw the stock initially decline more than 5% before rebounding over 2%, reflecting the market’s tug-of-war between strong guidance and the GAAP loss plus valuation concerns.

Detailed Breakdown

  1. Overall Revenue and Profit Performance
    • Net revenue: $1.01 billion (approximately $1.0063 billion), up about 109% year-over-year (from $480.7 million in the prior-year period), above market expectations of roughly $988 million (beat by ~2%).
    • Non-GAAP adjusted EPS: $3.23, up 267% year-over-year, above the $2.97 consensus (beat by ~9%).
    • Non-GAAP gross margin: 50.4%, up 1,260 basis points year-over-year.
    • Non-GAAP operating margin: 36.6%, up 2,160 basis points year-over-year.
    • Adjusted EBITDA: $406.4 million, corresponding to a margin of approximately 40%.
    • Non-GAAP net income: $326.3 million, up 415% year-over-year.
    • GAAP net loss: approximately $7.2 billion ($84.65 per share), primarily driven by a one-time non-cash loss on debt extinguishment of about $7.8 billion from the equitization of certain convertible notes.
    • Full-year FY2026 net revenue: approximately $3.01 billion, up about 83% year-over-year.
  2. Components Business Performance
    • Revenue: $649.4 million, up approximately 103% year-over-year (from $320.4 million), above the $636.9 million estimate.
    • Accounted for more than 60% of total revenue and remained the primary revenue base.
    • Key drivers: Strong AI data-center demand for scale-out and scale-across applications, including record 100G/200G EML shipments (200G EMLs exceeding 25% of total EML revenue), growing demand for ultra-high-power CPO lasers, continued sequential growth in narrow-linewidth lasers, and pump lasers up about 80% year-over-year.
  3. Other Business Segment Performance (Systems)
    • Systems revenue: $356.9 million, up approximately 123% year-over-year (from $160.3 million), above the $350.4 million estimate.
    • Growth rate exceeded that of the components business, indicating demand spillover from discrete devices to system-level solutions.
    • Key drivers: Cloud module business (record 800G transceiver shipments and initial volume production of 1.6T modules) and optical circuit switch (OCS) solutions beginning to contribute incremental revenue.
  4. Future Plans and Growth Drivers
    • CEO Michael Hurlston noted that OCS solutions and the cloud module business have started contributing incremental growth. Rising demand for ultra-high-power CPO lasers, an initial order for ELS modules, and broad NPO engagements signal that optics are beginning to penetrate in-rack connectivity, significantly expanding the optical technology total addressable market (TAM).
    • The company stated it is reaching its target operating model more than a quarter ahead of schedule, driven by faster-than-expected revenue scale, product mix improvement, and operating leverage.
    • Increasing AI compute workloads in both speed and bandwidth are prompting data-center architects to adopt optical links as a primary means of connectivity.
  5. Next-Quarter Guidance (FY2027 Q1)
    • Revenue: $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion (midpoint approximately $1.25 billion), representing about 135% year-over-year growth and roughly 24% sequential growth, approximately 8% above the market consensus of about $1.16 billion.
    • Non-GAAP adjusted EPS: $4.05 to $4.35 (midpoint approximately $4.20), up about 282% year-over-year and roughly 30% sequentially, about 16% above the $3.61 consensus.
    • Non-GAAP operating margin: 39.5% to 40.5% (midpoint approximately 40%), an improvement of about 340 basis points from the 36.6% reported in Q4.
  6. Market Context and Investor Concerns
    • Core tension: Robust AI optical communications demand (particularly data-center optical modules, lasers, and OCS) and significantly better-than-expected guidance support fundamental upside; however, the large GAAP non-cash loss, previously elevated expectations, and high valuation create near-term pressure and profit-taking risk.
    • Stock reaction: The shares closed up nearly 0.9% before the report; after-hours trading initially declined more than 5% before recovering to a gain of over 2%, reflecting competing forces.
    • Key items to watch going forward: Delivery against Q1 guidance, sustainability of operating margins near 40%, the pace at which CPO/ELS/NPO-related demand converts from early orders into scaled revenue, and whether supply constraints (especially in OCS and certain lasers) ease.

results.content:

NVIDIA partnered with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to establish independent financing platforms mobilizing over $500 billion in third-party capital specifically for AI data center construction and GPU procurement. The large-scale backing directly eases prior market concerns over AI financing sustainability.

🎯 Beneficiaries: NVDA, CRWV, SMCI; Key Catalyst: AI infrastructure funding channels open; watch NVDA volume and related infrastructure names for follow-through.

CoreWeave reported Q2 revenue of $2.58 billion (doubled year-over-year), a smaller-than-expected adjusted loss, and a revenue backlog of $104.2 billion, plus more than $25 billion in additional new commitments already secured. The company raised full-year guidance as management highlighted the start of operating leverage from scale. 

🎯 Beneficiaries: CRWV, NVDA, VST; Key Catalyst: AI cloud demand validated; monitor post-earnings follow-through and guidance delivery.

3. Super Micro Profit Surges as Gross Margin Sharply Recovers

SMCI posted Q4 revenue of $11.1 billion (+93% YoY), net income of $1.178 billion (vs. $195 million a year ago), and gross margin of 17.5%. Full-year revenue reached $39.1 billion with FY2027 guidance of $65–72 billion; management cited more than $60 billion in new orders and a record backlog.

🎯 Beneficiaries: SMCI, NVDA, AVGO; Key Catalyst: AI server demand and profitability dual confirmation; watch pre-market and intraday volatility.

4. Riot Platforms Secures $9.1 Billion Anthropic Compute Lease

Bitcoin miner Riot Platforms signed a 20-year, 191 MW IT capacity lease with a “leading frontier AI lab” (Bloomberg identifies Anthropic) valued at approximately $9.1 billion (up to $16.1 billion with extensions). First 96 MW is targeted for delivery by end-2027 as the company pivots from mining to AI data-center landlord.

🎯 Beneficiaries: RIOT, MARA, CORZ; Key Catalyst: Miner-to-AI-infra transition lands; watch power and data-center related sentiment spillover.

Intel increased its previously announced common stock offering from $15 billion to $20 billion, priced around $95 per share, to fund AI compute-related capital expenditures and foundry expansion. The company had already raised its capex outlook on strong AI demand. 

🎯 Beneficiaries: INTC, AMKR, TSM; Key Catalyst: AI foundry and advanced packaging funding secured; watch dilution impact versus capacity progress.

Trading Note: Focus remains on AI infrastructure financing rollout and CoreWeave/SMCI earnings confirmation, with capital continuing to flow toward data centers and compute leasing. Watch tonight’s CPI data and Cisco earnings; manage position size with volume and volatility in mind. U.S. equity volatility has increased recently. results.title: Bitget UEX Daily | Fed Officials Turn Hawkish Again, CPI May Set September Path; US-Iran Hormuz Stalemate Continues; Nvidia Clarifies Financing Plan, Easing Concerns (August 12, 2026)
results.content:
I. Hot News Highlights

Federal Reserve Dynamics

Fed officials turn hawkish again; tonight’s CPI becomes key basis for September hike pricing

  • Chicago Fed President Goolsbee emphasized that rapidly rising prices are currently the biggest problem facing the U.S. economy, while the labor market is “stable but not strong.”
  • Cleveland Fed President Hammack stated that the Fed may need multiple rate hikes to bring inflation back to the 2% target.
  • Markets are focused on the U.S. July CPI report due Wednesday evening Beijing time, with expectations of 3.4% YoY headline and 2.5% core; CME data shows roughly equal odds for a September hold versus a hike. Market Impact: Hawkish comments ahead of critical inflation data are pressuring short-end rate-sensitive assets and keeping risk appetite cautious. The CPI outcome will directly influence September policy pricing.

International Commodities

US-Iran maritime conflict escalates; Hormuz Strait stalemate continues

  • Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Rezaei said the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen unless the U.S. accepts Iran’s ceasefire conditions (including unfreezing Iranian assets and ending related regional conflicts).
  • The U.S. military fired a missile at a Panama-flagged cargo ship heading to an Iranian port in the Gulf of Oman; Houthi forces attacked Saudi and Egyptian vessels in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, causing crew fatalities. Market Impact: Geopolitical risk premiums are supporting oil prices, supply disruption concerns persist, and inflation expectations are intertwining with safe-haven demand, increasing near-term commodity volatility.

Macroeconomic Policy

Market sentiment remains pessimistic; historical data points to potential rebound space

  • The S&P 500 has repeatedly hit new highs, yet shorts outnumbered longs in 20 of the past 25 weeks, with institutional positioning lagging fundamental improvement.
  • 22V Research noted that excessive pessimism has historically foreshadowed positive returns over the following 1–6 months; Wells Fargo’s sentiment indicator is approaching extreme bullish levels that have previously triggered sell signals. Market Impact: The disconnect between sentiment and fundamentals may provide room for a later recovery, but the near term remains constrained by both CPI and geopolitics.

II. Market Review

Commodities & Forex Performance

  • Spot Gold: Approx. $4,390/oz, +0.52%
  • Spot Silver: Approx. $65.0/oz, +0.5%
  • WTI Crude: Approx. $83.9/bbl, +0.96%
  • Brent Crude: Approx. $85/bbl, +0.67%
  • US Dollar Index (DXY): 99.86, +0.05%

Driver Analysis: The US-Iran Hormuz stalemate and Houthi attacks continue to support oil prices and sustain geopolitical risk premiums. Gold is oscillating between inflation-data anticipation and safe-haven demand, while silver is influenced more by its industrial attributes. Hawkish Fed comments are limiting upside for precious metals. Institutional views hold that near-term commodities remain driven by geopolitics and the upcoming CPI; elevated oil prices may reinforce sticky-inflation concerns, creating a linkage of geopolitical tension → oil support → inflation expectations → interest-rate path re-pricing.

Cryptocurrency Performance

  • Bitget BTC/USDT Liquidation Map: BTC currently around $63,711. Dense long liquidations are concentrated near $63,000–$63,500; a break below $63,000 could accelerate long liquidations. Short liquidations cluster in the $64,000–$65,000 zone; a break above $64,000 could trigger successive short covering and push prices higher.

  • BTC Spot ETF Net Flows: Yesterday net outflow of $145 million; today’s dynamic net outflow $42.4 million

Driver Analysis: Softening equity risk appetite and rising oil prices have heightened inflation concerns, exerting macro pressure on crypto. BTC failed to hold the $64,000 level, while ETH showed relative resilience. Liquidations were dominated by longs, reflecting stop-loss pressure after the upside failed. Institutional consensus points to a range-bound, mildly weak bias, with focus on tonight’s CPI transmission to risk assets and ETF flow changes.

US Equity Index Performance

  • Dow Jones: Closed at 53,791.85, -0.34%, second consecutive daily decline
  • S&P 500: Closed at 7,728.20, -0.32%

Performance Summary & Driver Analysis: The Mag 7 showed clear divergence. Google and Amazon led the declines, with Apple and Microsoft also lower; Meta and Tesla closed higher against the trend. Nvidia’s decline narrowed after Jensen Huang clarified the financing plan. Overall pressure stemmed from the US-Iran stalemate and hawkish Fed comments, as the market shifted from pure AI thematic trading toward re-pricing of capital-expenditure efficiency and macro risks, producing differentiated individual-stock drivers.

Sector Movers Observation

Semiconductors / Memory – Relatively resilient with partial rebound

  • Representative stocks: SK Hynix +approx. 4.7%, Micron +approx. 0.87%, KLA +approx. 4.0%.
  • Drivers: AI compute demand logic remains intact; capital rotated back into selected hardware names amid the broader pullback.

Optical Communication – Overall strength

Cloud Computing Service Providers – Higher

  • Drivers: Capital returned to compute leasing and AI infrastructure themes.

III. In-Depth US Equity Analysis

1. Nvidia (NVDA) – Jensen Huang Clarifies Financing Plan, Easing Concerns

Event Overview: The market had previously misunderstood Nvidia’s potential $500 billion compute financing plan. Jensen Huang clarified on X that support would be capped at no more than 25% of any single project opportunity and would be limited, residual-value-based support intended to supplement rather than replace independent underwriters. The clarification removed uncertainty and caused the 5-year CDS to tighten. Separately, Nvidia is reportedly developing a trillion-parameter open-source model, Nemotron 4, aimed at expanding the open-source ecosystem and driving GPU demand. CME plans to launch GPU compute futures. Market Interpretation: Institutions believe the clarification significantly reduced credit-risk concerns, shifting the narrative from “unlimited exposure” to limited support. Analysts will monitor the actual operation of the financing platform and the pull from the open-source model on the ecosystem. Investment Implications: Near-term sentiment repair is constructive; the medium-term thesis still requires tracking AI capex returns and supply-chain execution.

2. Google (GOOGL) – Largest Decline Among Mag 7; Capex Efficiency in Focus

Event Overview: Google shares fell approximately 3.84%, the largest drop among the Mag 7. The market continues to digest earlier capex increases and the pace of AI investment returns. Market Interpretation: Under hawkish macro conditions and geopolitical uncertainty, institutions remain cautious on high-capex tech names, emphasizing the match between cloud growth and investment efficiency. Investment Implications: Watch subsequent earnings for AI revenue contribution and any changes to capex guidance.

3. Apple (AAPL) – Followed Tech Sector Lower

Event Overview: Apple declined approximately 1.09%, moving with the broader tech adjustment. Markets continue to assess its positioning within the AI and hardware cycle. Market Interpretation: Relatively defensive but still dragged by sector sentiment; institutions are monitoring the iPhone cycle and services resilience. Investment Implications: As a relatively defensive tech allocation, track new-product launches and AI feature rollout progress.

4. Meta (META) – Closed Higher Against the Trend

Event Overview: Meta rose approximately 0.71%, showing relative strength among the Mag 7. Market Interpretation: Institutions may be relatively constructive on advertising and AI efficiency improvements, with some short-term capital returning. Investment Implications: Monitor marginal improvements in the advertising business and AI investment signals.

5. Tesla (TSLA) – Modest Gain

Event Overview: Tesla rose approximately 0.58%, showing resilience in an overall pressured environment. Market Interpretation: Markets remain divided on delivery momentum and the AI/robotics narrative; the near-term move appears more driven by stock-specific flows. Investment Implications: High volatility; track actual Robotaxi and energy-business progress.

IV. Market & Project Updates

  1. U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) Short-Term Energy Outlook: Raised 2026 WTI price forecast to $80.88/bbl (from $76.26) and 2027 to $65.39 (from $60.76). Raised 2026 Brent forecast to $86.81/bbl (from $81.91) and 2027 to $69.39 (from $64.76).
  2. South Korea’s Kiwoom Securities simultaneously lowered target prices for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Growing concerns that the general memory-chip cycle has peaked (peak-out) have prompted more brokerages to cut targets for the two Korean leaders. Kiwoom cut Samsung’s target from 390,000 won to 350,000 won and SK Hynix from 2.2 million won to 2.1 million won, while maintaining “Buy” ratings on both.
  3. According to Fox Business, Strategy CEO Phong Le said the company will resume purchasing more bitcoin for the remainder of the year.
  4. Pokémon trading cards have outperformed both the S&P 500 and Bitcoin year-to-date. Meanwhile, a group of emerging blockchain platforms is betting on tokenization to transform the roughly $13–15 billion collectibles market by improving liquidity, ownership records, and settlement efficiency for physical collectibles.
  5. Bloomberg senior ETF analyst Eric Balchunas noted that converting bitcoin into physical spot bitcoin ETF shares does not currently trigger capital-gains recognition; the original cost basis and holding period carry over, effectively deferring rather than avoiding tax. The same mechanism can operate in reverse (ETF shares into bitcoin).

V. Today’s Market Calendar

Data Release Schedule

Evening United States July CPI (Headline/Core) ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
 

Key Event Preview

August 12 (Wednesday)

  1. ★★★★★ U.S. July CPI release (market expects headline YoY ~3.4% vs. prior 3.5%; core YoY ~2.5% vs. prior 2.6%; MoM headline ~0.1%, core ~0.2%). This is the most important macro data of the week after last week’s non-farm payrolls and directly affects September Fed hike pricing (current implied probability ~44%).
  2. Tencent Holdings reports earnings (focus on games, advertising, fintech, and AI capex / Hunyuan progress).

Institutional Views

results.title: Big Tech’s AI Arms Race: Hundreds of Billions in CapEx Surge, the J-Curve of Returns, and Investment Logic Unpacked
results.content:
Core Summary
2026 marks the peak year of AI infrastructure investment. The combined CapEx of Microsoft, Amazon, Google (Alphabet), and Meta has been revised upward to  $690–745 billion , a surge of more than 70% year-over-year, with cumulative spending already exceeding $1.1 trillion. Near-term free cash flow is under pressure and the market has grown increasingly sensitive to higher spending guidance, yet the long-term J-curve of returns remains intact — profits are steadily flowing from the model layer into hardware and infrastructure. Because the marginal cost of AI is not zero, the push to squeeze hardware efficiency will continue for a long time. For traders, the most verifiable and high-beta opportunities still lie in the physical bottlenecks: GPUs, advanced packaging, HBM, optical modules, and power & cooling.
 
 
I. Scale of the Race: A Historic Infrastructure Wave Still Accelerating
In 2026, the AI arms race among tech giants has reached new heights. The four companies — Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta — have guided combined capital expenditure of approximately $690–745 billion, up more than 70% from roughly $410 billion in 2025. Recent earnings have further confirmed or raised parts of this guidance:
  • Amazon: ~$200 billion (largest in absolute terms)
  • Microsoft: ~$190 billion
  • Alphabet: raised to $195–205 billion (Q2 actual spend already $44.9 billion, with management explicitly signaling a significant further increase in 2027)
  • Meta: $125–145 billion (some updates lifted the lower end to around $130 billion)
The bulk of this capital is flowing into high-end AI chips, hyperscale data centers, power and cooling infrastructure, advanced packaging, top talent, and frontier model training. Nvidia continues to benefit as the core GPU supplier, with its data-center business still growing explosively. TSMC firmly controls the critical advanced-node process technology and CoWoS advanced packaging capacity.
At the same time, the giants are accelerating in-house chip development (Google’s TPU, Amazon’s Trainium, Meta’s custom silicon) to reduce reliance on any single supplier.
This is no longer merely a hardware contest. It has become a full-spectrum competition spanning infrastructure, models, talent ecosystems, and compute dominance — one of the largest technology infrastructure build-outs in human history. By the end of June 2026, the four companies’ cumulative CapEx since the start of the AI boom had already surpassed $1.1 trillion.
 
II. The J-Curve of Returns: Long-Term Upside vs. Near-Term Pressure — Profits Flowing from Models to Hardware
The return profile of this massive front-loaded investment clearly exhibits a classic “J-curve”: heavy early outlays, delayed payback, but substantial long-term potential.
  • Microsoft: Azure growth remains strong (in the 40%+ range) with relatively high AI revenue visibility; free cash flow improvement is expected to lead the group.
  • Amazon: AWS growth is solid and backlog is ample, yet free cash flow faces the most pronounced pressure in 2026; the majority of returns are expected to materialize in 2027–2028 as new capacity comes online.
  • Alphabet: Cloud growth is extremely rapid (Q2 Cloud revenue up ~80% year-over-year), but intense investment has already pushed quarterly free cash flow into negative territory; pressure may become more visible around early 2027.
  • Meta: Returns are captured more indirectly through improved ad targeting and user experience. ROI attribution is relatively opaque, and cash-flow pressure may last longer than peers.
Overall timeline: 2026 is the peak investment and cash-flow stress year. Scaled returns are expected to emerge between 2027 and 2029, depending on data-center utilization rates, AI service pricing power, and enterprise willingness to pay.
Key Insight: The model layer struggles to build lasting network effects and is more likely to compete like a commodity on cost and efficiency. Because the marginal cost of AI is not zero, profits will continue flowing from the model layer into hardware, cloud, and infrastructure. The drive to squeeze hardware efficiency and invest in physical compute will persist for a long time.
III. Diverging Market Sentiment: From “Buying the Narrative” to “Validating Returns”
Market reactions are becoming increasingly polarized:
  • Bull case: Clear long-term growth trajectory, high order visibility, and expanding platform moats in the AI era. Cloud growth rates and backlogs continue to validate demand.
  • Bear case: Near-term gross-margin compression, free-cash-flow erosion, rising depreciation burden, and rapid balance-sheet expansion (debt and long-term lease commitments rising sharply). After recent earnings (especially Alphabet’s), the market’s tolerance for higher CapEx guidance has clearly declined, and stock prices have become more sensitive to upward revisions.
Recent results show that free cash flow is no longer the sole metric that matters. Debt leverage — particularly approaching the 1x net-debt credit threshold — and actual utilization rates have become the new focal points. Until those critical leverage thresholds are reached, CapEx is more likely to keep accelerating than to slow down.
IV. Clear Winners and Sectors to Watch
The most transparent beneficiaries remain concentrated in the AI supply chain:
 
Segment Key Names Driver Logic
GPUs & Chip Design Nvidia, AMD Explosive data-center demand
Advanced Foundry TSMC Monopoly on leading-edge nodes & CoWoS
High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Micron, SK Hynix Memory bottleneck for AI training
Optical Interconnects / Modules Marvell, Lumentum Data-center network upgrades
Servers & Infrastructure Dell, Super Micro Hyperscaler capacity expansion
Power & Cooling Vertiv, Eaton Energy and thermal constraints

results.title: Lumentum Q4 Earnings Preview: Orders Booked Through 2028 — Can Growth Deliver Amid Capacity Shortages and the Optical Module Ban?
results.content:
1. Investment Highlights Overview

Lumentum (LITE.US) will report its fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter and full-year results after the U.S. market close on August 11. Wall Street consensus expects Q4 revenue of approximately $988 million (+105.5% YoY) and GAAP EPS of about $2.35 (-20.7% YoY). The company’s prior guidance calls for revenue of $960 million–$1.01 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $2.85–$3.05. What the market is truly focused on is not a single earnings metric, but order visibility, gross margin trends, the ramp of new products, and management’s comments on the potential “China optical module ban.”

2. Four Key Focus Areas

Focus 1: 1.6T Optical Module and CPO Ramp Progress

The company has confirmed that 1.6T optical modules will enter volume production this quarter, with CPO-related products scheduled to begin volume shipments to customers including NVIDIA in the second half of 2026. Investors will closely watch the actual revenue contribution, gross margin profile, and smoothness of the production ramp. Progress at or above expectations would reinforce the company’s long-term growth narrative in AI high-speed interconnects.

Focus 2: OCS Business Volume Ramp and Order Fulfillment

Optical Circuit Switch (OCS) is viewed as a key long-term growth driver. Order backlog has surpassed $400 million, and the company targets $100 million in quarterly revenue by the end of 2026. Attention will center on delivery progress, new customer wins, and whether supply-chain constraints continue to limit shipment pace.

Focus 3: Capacity Shortage and Indium Phosphide Supply Reality

Management previously stated that orders are already booked through 2028, with current supply shortfalls for EML lasers, pump lasers, and related products exceeding 30%. Indium phosphide-based lasers remain the most constrained link in the supply chain. The production timeline for the new North Carolina factory and the role of long-term contracts in supporting capital expenditure will be key topics on the earnings call. Whether capacity can keep pace with demand will directly determine the upper limit of growth elasticity.

Focus 4: Optical Module Ban Narrative and Management Commentary

Following the August 4 Reuters report that the Trump administration was drafting a ban on imports of certain Chinese optical modules, the stock surged nearly 9% as the market priced in a potential share shift from Chinese to U.S. suppliers. However, Chinese manufacturers still account for more than 60% of global high-speed optical module capacity, and Lumentum itself remains partially dependent on China for indium phosphide raw materials. If management only highlights improved near-term demand visibility while reiterating capacity and supply constraints, the positive impact may be limited. Clearer comments on customer qualification windows and long-term industry restructuring could amplify the narrative.

3. Risks and Opportunities

Upside Catalysts:

  • Revenue lands at the high end of guidance or exceeds expectations, accompanied by constructive commentary on the next quarter or full-year outlook.
  • 1.6T/CPO shipments ramp faster than expected and OCS deliveries accelerate, validating new product elasticity.
  • Management offers an optimistic assessment of the ban’s impact, combined with a clear capacity-expansion timeline, reinforcing the “beneficiary” narrative.

Downside Risks:

  • Revenue only meets the midpoint of guidance or falls slightly short, with signs of margin or expense pressure that raise questions about the quality of expansion.
  • Capacity bottlenecks remain unresolved, new-product ramps lag expectations, or raw-material constraints are re-emphasized.
  • The ban is ultimately framed as highly uncertain (possible exemptions, modifications, or delays), leading to a unwind of previously priced-in benefits.

4. Trading Strategy Considerations

Bull Case: If core revenue and non-GAAP profitability clearly beat consensus, new-product contributions exceed expectations, and management provides constructive guidance along with confidence in capacity expansion, the company’s position as an AI optical “picks-and-shovels” play could be reinforced, supporting valuation recovery. Bear Case: If results merely meet or slightly miss expectations, capacity and supply-chain constraints are repeatedly highlighted, or ban-related commentary turns cautious, profit-taking could follow—especially given that policy expectations have already been largely priced in.

Key Metrics to Watch:

  • Total revenue and whether it reaches the upper end of guidance
  • Non-GAAP gross margin and operating margin trends
  • Specific contribution or guidance for 1.6T/CPO and OCS businesses
  • Whether full-year or next-quarter revenue/profit outlook is raised
  • Commentary on capacity shortage and new factory timeline

Trading Notes: If results beat and guidance is constructive, consider opportunities on any pullback. If data is in-line or management tone is cautious, be mindful of near-term volatility and avoid chasing. Position sizing and stop-loss levels should be adjusted according to individual risk tolerance.

results.title: Rocket Lab Q2 2026 Earnings Highlights: Record Revenue of $234 Million, Up 62% YoY; Backlog Reaches Record $2.36 Billion; Strong Q3 Guidance
results.content:
Core View

Rocket Lab (RKLB) reported its second-quarter 2026 results, with revenue reaching a record $234 million, up 62% year-over-year and beating market expectations. Net loss narrowed to approximately $49.26 million, or a diluted loss per share of $0.08. Backlog hit a record $2.36 billion, up 137% year-over-year. Growth was primarily driven by the Space Systems segment (accounting for about 81% of revenue), while Launch Services revenue fluctuated due to revenue recognition timing. The company guided Q3 revenue of $250–265 million (above Wall Street estimates), but gross margin guidance came in below expectations, reflecting margin pressure from the expansion of lower-margin satellite platforms. Shares declined after the report.

Detailed Breakdown

  1. Overall Revenue and Profit Performance
    • Quarterly revenue of $234 million (approximately $234.066 million), up 62% year-over-year (from $144.5 million), and up about 16.8% sequentially, exceeding the prior quarter’s record by $34 million and beating analyst estimates (around $231.4–232 million).
    • Net loss of approximately $49.26 million, narrowed from $66.41 million in the year-ago period; diluted loss per share of $0.08 (versus $0.13 a year earlier), slightly wider than some estimates of a $0.06–0.07 loss.
    • Product revenue approximately $181.3 million; service revenue approximately $52.7 million. Overall gross margin around 36%, improved year-over-year.
    • First-half 2026 revenue of $434.4 million, up about 63% year-over-year; first-half net loss of approximately $94.28 million, improved from the prior year.
  2. Space Systems Performance
    • Revenue of $189.5 million, up approximately 94% year-over-year and 38.6% sequentially, representing the largest revenue contributor (about 81% of Q2 total revenue).
    • Growth driven primarily by expansion in satellite manufacturing and initial contribution from the Mynaric acquisition.
    • Key contracts secured: approximately $397 million award to deliver multiple Flatellite spacecraft for the U.S. Space Force’s SB-AMTI program (to be launched on Neutron); more than $160 million across two contracts to build three geostationary satellites, including a prime contract with the U.S. Space Force’s Space Systems Command to build and operate two space domain awareness satellites.
    • Formally established Rocket Lab Germany GmbH to support scaling of satellite and component manufacturing in Germany and to provide commercial and sovereign space capabilities to European customers.
  3. Launch Services and Other Business Performance
    • Launch Services revenue of $44.6 million, down approximately 4% year-over-year and 30% sequentially (despite a similar number of launches), primarily due to the mix of point-in-time Electron revenue recognition versus over-time HASTE recognition.
    • More than $437 million in new launch contracts secured across Electron, HASTE, and Neutron during Q2 and post-quarter, expanding the total launch backlog to a record of more than 90 missions.
    • Overall backlog of $2.36 billion (roughly 40% Launch Services / 60% Space Systems), up 137% year-over-year.
    • Introduced the GHOST globally deployable launch system; first site (Launch Complex 4) at the Pacific Spaceport Complex in Kodiak, Alaska, with planned suborbital debut in 2027.
  4. Future Plans and Strategic Initiatives
    • Neutron medium-lift reusable rocket: Progress on assembly, integration, and first-flight hardware testing; Stage 1 tank production remains on track for delivery to the launch pad in Q4 2026 (with some adjustment to earlier inaugural flight expectations).
    • Closed the acquisitions of Mynaric and Motiv; announced a landmark agreement to acquire Iridium Communications Inc. to create a fully vertically integrated space company capable of designing, building, launching, and operating its own satellite constellations.
    • Continued investment in launch infrastructure, production capacity, and Neutron development; additional Neutron launch contracts signed (including with Kepler Communications).
  5. Q3 2026 Guidance
    • Revenue: $250 million to $265 million (midpoint approximately $257.5 million, above Wall Street estimates of around $238.5 million).
    • GAAP gross margin: 29% to 31% (below analyst average estimate of approximately 37.6%); non-GAAP gross margin: 35% to 37%.
    • GAAP operating expenses: $143 million to $149 million; non-GAAP operating expenses: $121 million to $127 million.
    • Net interest income: $21 million.
    • Adjusted EBITDA loss: $17 million to $23 million.
    • Basic weighted-average shares outstanding: approximately 641 million (including about 41 million Series A convertible preferred shares).
    • The company noted that more than $1 billion in new launch and space systems contracts have already been signed in Q3 to date, supporting the strong growth outlook.
  6. Market Context and Investor Concerns
    • The core tension is strong top-line growth and record backlog (driven by surging demand) versus near-term margin pressure: the rising mix of lower-margin satellite platforms is weighing on profitability, leading to Q3 gross margin guidance below expectations.
    • Investor attention is also focused on Neutron development progress and the adjusted timeline for first flight, alongside ongoing high spending on R&D and infrastructure.
    • Market reaction: Shares closed down approximately 3.37%, with further pressure in after-hours trading (reports of declines exceeding 7–8%), reflecting caution on short-term profitability.
    • Positive factors include growing defense and government contracts, the vertical integration strategy via the proposed Iridium transaction, and expansion of the launch backlog, which support longer-term competitive differentiation.

results.title: Responding to the “$500 billion financing question”! Jensen Huang: Nvidia’s “AI factories” are becoming “investment-grade assets”; real demand exists and it is definitely not “circular financing”
results.content:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has personally stepped in to endorse the company's plan to mobilize over $500 billion in AI infrastructure financing in partnership with six major financial institutions. He made it clear that Nvidia's AI factory computing power is becoming an investable asset class, with demand stemming from real business scenarios. Independent institutional investors will conduct due diligence on each project separately, dismissing external doubts of "circular financing."

On August 10, Jensen Huang announced on social platform X that Nvidia had reached agreements with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to jointly establish an independent financing platform, with the aim to mobilize over $500 billion in third-party capital over time to support AI infrastructure construction. He emphasized that the $500 billion refers to the total amount of third-party capital that the above platforms are designed to mobilize, “neither Nvidia’s revenue nor a commitment by a single fund or to a single customer.”

After the announcement, Nvidia’s stock price fell by as much as 3.2%. The price of the 5-year Credit Default Swap (CDS) measuring the company's credit risk rose to 77.215 basis points on Monday, about 5.3 basis points higher than the previous trading day, the largest single-day gain in two weeks. Analysts believe that this reflects the market's growing attention to Nvidia’s potential credit risk amid such massive financing models.

Wallstreetcn article previously reported, quoting sources from the Financial Times, that Nvidia is looking to jointly raise up to $500 billion with Wall Street giants Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock’s GIP, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR as a consortium for AI infrastructure projects, covering AI chip procurement, power production, and data center construction.

Following related reports, "Dr. Doom" Jim Chanos posted a sarcastic comment on Nvidia’s joint AI infrastructure financing with Blackstone and other financial giants, likening it to the financial engineering of the 2008 financial crisis, and implying that if the AI bubble bursts, the parties involved may repeat the fate of Wall Street executives being questioned by Congress at that time.

AI Factory: From "Buying Chips" to "Financeable Infrastructure"

In his post, Jensen Huang systematically explained the asset logic behind Nvidia’s AI factory, seeking to redefine the market’s perception of this business model.

He stated that the AI industry has moved from the era where enterprises purchased chips project by project and built their own data centers to a new stage where AI factories can be financed as productive infrastructure—with replicable platforms, long-term institutional capital support, and a diversified customer base using computing power to generate revenue.

Jensen Huang emphasized that Nvidia's computing power is not merely chips, but a comprehensive AI factory platform that includes accelerated computing, networking, system software, AI frameworks, and a global developer ecosystem.

He pointed out that a single Nvidia AI factory can simultaneously serve multiple customers and workloads, offering flexibility and interchangeability; when the needs of one customer change, the factory can be used by another customer, another cloud provider, or another operator, "This broad ecosystem gives Nvidia’s computing power a vast potential user market, helping to protect residual value."

Huang characterized the above collaboration as "the beginning of open capital markets for AI infrastructure." He stated, these financial institutions are all leading global infrastructure investors with deep expertise in underwriting long-term productive assets; together, both sides will build a replicable financing platform to support the factories needed for the AI ecosystem.

CUDA Software Continues to Appreciate, A100 Still in Commercial Use Six Years On

Jensen Huang focused on the long-term economic value of Nvidia’s computing assets, supported by concrete data.

He explained that CUDA software continues to enhance the performance, efficiency, and total ownership cost of installed infrastructure, allowing AI factories to deliver more intelligence at lower cost throughout their lifecycle, thereby extending their economic value.

Taking the A100 as an example: Nvidia launched the Ampere-based A100 in 2020, and six years later it remains commercially active in AI training, fine-tuning, inference, and high-performance computing, with clients continuing to sign multi-year capacity deals. "The economic life of A100 is extending toward ten years."

On GPU rental pricing, Huang cited market data showing that the H100 one-year rental price has risen from about $1.70 per GPU hour in October 2025 to about $2.35 in March 2026; median cross-provider on-demand pricing increased from about $2.00 per GPU hour in October 2025 to $2.70 in June 2026. The Blackwell series commands an even greater premium, with B200 cloud prices at about $5.30 to $7.05 per GPU hour.

He believes the above data demonstrates the lasting economic value of Nvidia’s computing power.

Direct Response to "Circular Financing" Doubts

Addressing the market’s main concern over "circular financing," Jensen Huang set up a Q&A section in his article to respond directly.

He said the very design of this financing arrangement is intended to address this concern. Demand comes from leading AI labs, AI-native startups, enterprise customers, cloud providers, and countries building AI services—“the demand is real.” Each capital provider will independently conduct due diligence on every project, evaluating client credentials, demand, utilization, cash flow, and residual value. "Nvidia provides the platform, and investors make independent financing decisions."

Regarding Nvidia’s own risk exposure, Huang revealed that in some cases, Nvidia may provide up to 25% residual value support for a single project, "prudently assessed project-by-project." He emphasized this ratio is “far lower than other computing power financing arrangements” and is supplemental rather than a substitute for independent due diligence.

Jensen Huang concluded by placing the construction of AI factories in a broader historical context. He stated that every industrial revolution has been built on infrastructure—electricity, transportation, communications, and computing—and each phase has relied on external financing. "AI factories are the infrastructure of the intelligent era."

He summarized the business logic of AI as a positive feedback loop: Companies use AI to write software, develop drugs, design products, serve customers, automate operations, and build new services; more computing power brings better AI, better AI leads to more usage, more usage brings more revenue, and more revenue drives further investment into computing power.

"This is the virtuous cycle of the AI industrial revolution."

Jensen Huang stated that through this collaboration, Nvidia and the world's leading financial institutions will jointly provide infrastructure financing for this industrial revolution, making AI factories more accessible to businesses, industries, and nations.

Wallstreetcn article also noted that this cooperation is not Nvidia’s first deep involvement in AI industry chain financing.

Previous reports indicated that Nvidia was in talks to provide up to $25 billion in credit guarantees for OpenAI and was discussing financing $350 billion for OpenAI’s chip procurement plan; last month Nvidia also announced an expanded partnership with South Korea’s SK Group, with total business volume expected to exceed $500 billion. These moves show that Nvidia is gradually transitioning from a chip supplier to the capital mobilization core of the AI infrastructure ecosystem.

"Dr. Doom" Draws Parallels to 2008: Next Congressional Hearing?

Simultaneously with Huang’s post, Wall Street’s famous short seller, also known as “Dr. Doom,” James Chanos, shared a thought-provoking comment on social media. He wrote:

“These guys’ next time sitting at the same table explaining AI financing could well be at a Congressional hearing in 2031…”

Chanos’s implication references the 2008 financial crisis—at the time, executives from major Wall Street financial institutions were forced to attend Congressional hearings due to the systemic risks posed by subprime mortgages, credit default swaps, and CDOs. He compared Nvidia’s joint financing arrangement with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to those financial engineering operations, suggesting that if the AI infrastructure investment bubble pops in a few years, Jensen Huang and these financial executives may together face Congressional inquiries.

Notably, when someone in the comments below his post asked if the parties involved would face criminal charges, Chanos clarified: “No one said anything about going to jail.”

1. Investment Highlights Overview

Rocket Lab is scheduled to report its second-quarter 2026 results after the U.S. market close on August 10, 2026. Wall Street consensus expects revenue of approximately $231–232 million (+59.8%–60% YoY), within the company’s own guidance range of $225–240 million. Adjusted EPS is expected in the range of -$0.06 to -$0.08, reflecting a meaningful narrowing of losses versus the prior-year period. Investors will focus on Electron launch cadence and success rates, Neutron first-flight timeline, and progress on the roughly $8 billion Iridium Communications acquisition. Recent large defense contract wins combined with broader space-sector sentiment swings make this print a key test of growth durability and valuation support.

2. Four Key Focus Areas

Focus 1: Launch Services — Electron Cadence and Neutron First-Flight Timeline

Launch activity remains the core near-term driver. The market will scrutinize the number of Electron missions flown, success rates, and per-launch contribution margins, while closely tracking Neutron development progress, engine testing, and the expected late-2026 first flight. Recent multi-hundred-million-dollar Space Force awards, including an approximately $397 million contract, and the assignment of a Neutron national-security mission with a 2028 deadline have raised expectations for medium-lift capability. Any upside in launch metrics or a reaffirmation of the Neutron schedule would strengthen visibility into the growth trajectory.

Focus 2: Space Systems Mix and Backlog Resilience

Space Systems (satellite manufacturing and components) typically carry higher gross margins than pure launch services, so its revenue contribution and delivery pace directly influence overall profitability. Backlog stood at a record roughly $2.2 billion at the end of Q1; investors will watch sequential order intake and conversion rates in Q2. Management previously guided Q2 GAAP gross margin to 33%–35%, slightly below Q1 levels due to a higher mix of lower-margin contracts. Confirmation that this is temporary rather than structural will be important for assessing the path to margin expansion.

Focus 3: Iridium Acquisition Progress and Valuation Re-rating Potential

The roughly $8 billion acquisition of Iridium, expected to close in mid-2027, is the most significant medium-term catalyst. It positions Rocket Lab to expand from hardware and launch into communications services and data subscriptions, bringing valuable spectrum and an existing customer base. Attention will center on integration timelines, preliminary commentary on revenue mix and margin implications, and any discussion of technical or commercial synergies (such as bundling launches with communications payloads). Positive integration language could support a shift toward higher, more service-oriented valuation multiples.

Focus 4: Full-Year Growth Sustainability and Guidance Updates

Rocket Lab has delivered successive record revenue quarters. A Q2 result near the midpoint of guidance that sustains approximately 60% year-over-year growth would continue that momentum. Markets will also watch for any update to full-year revenue expectations, the trajectory of adjusted EBITDA losses, and management’s tone on second-half launch and Space Systems delivery. In a high-volatility environment for technology and space stocks, guidance language often carries more weight than the single-quarter print itself.

3. Risks and Opportunities Coexist

Upside Catalysts:

  • Electron launch volume and success rates exceed expectations, or the Neutron first-flight timeline is firmly reaffirmed with additional bookings.
  • Revenue meaningfully beats the consensus midpoint while backlog continues to expand and gross margins outperform guidance.
  • Constructive updates on Iridium integration that outline a clear path to service-model synergies and valuation re-rating.

Downside Risks:

  • Softer-than-expected launch cadence or success rates, or any indication of delay in the Neutron schedule.
  • Results that merely meet the midpoint of guidance without an upward revision to the full-year outlook, or margin pressure that raises questions about earnings quality.
  • Spillover from SpaceX-related sector sentiment (elevated capital intensity and share unlocks) combined with high valuation scrutiny.

4. Trading Strategy Suggestions

Bull Case: Clear beats on revenue and launch metrics, resilient backlog, and constructive commentary on Neutron progress plus Iridium integration would reinforce the “commercial space leader + services transition” narrative and support valuation recovery.

Bear Case: In-line or slightly soft results, signs of growth deceleration, or cautious language around Neutron or the acquisition could trigger profit-taking, particularly given elevated options implied volatility (around the 100% level) and an expected post-earnings move of roughly ±15%.

Key Metrics to Watch:

  • Total revenue and year-over-year growth rate
  • Electron launch count, success rate, and Space Systems revenue mix
  • Backlog change and new contract awards
  • Neutron development updates and any full-year guidance revision
  • Gross margin and adjusted EBITDA performance

Trading Considerations: If results and guidance are constructive, look for pullbacks as potential entry points. If the print is uneventful or guidance is cautious, respect short-term volatility and avoid chasing. Position sizing and stop-loss levels should always reflect individual risk tolerance.

results.title: Raised earnings forecast but lowered target price, JPMorgan: Kioxia’s valuation depends on "the credibility of long-term contracts"
results.content:
Kioxia's profit forecast has been fully revised upward, but after its share price was halved, JPMorgan believes that genuine valuation recovery will have to wait until the market witnesses that long-term agreements "actually work" in practice.

According to Fast Trading Desk, JPMorgan's latest research report released on August 10 maintained an "Overweight" rating, simultaneously raising its profit forecast but lowering the target price from 155,000 yen (for the end of 2026) to 130,000 yen (for the end of 2027).

Profit upgrade: Pricing stronger than expected, eSSD as the core driver

JPMorgan’s core reason for the current upward adjustment is that recent NAND pricing has beaten expectations.

The specific revisions are as follows (all are operating profit):

  • FY2027: Raised from 741.88 billion yen to 800.21 billion yen, a year-on-year increase of about 9 times

  • FY2028: Raised from 1,056.25 billion yen to 1,124.10 billion yen, a year-on-year increase of about 40%

  • FY2029: Raised from 1,392.60 billion yen to 1,456.23 billion yen, a year-on-year increase of about 30%

There are three specific assumption adjustments behind these changes:

First, the timing for consumer-grade NAND price decline will be postponed—from the previously expected Q3 2027 to Q4 2027—reflecting tighter supply-demand dynamics.

Second, the eSSD (enterprise-grade solid-state drives) average price assumption was raised, mainly due to stronger-than-expected price recovery in Q2 2026. JPMorgan still expects that, as multi-year LTA gradually roll out from 2027, pricing will become more stable (with the company's target of 50% LTA coverage in 2028).

Third, the bit shipment forecast remains largely unchanged.

It is noteworthy that JPMorgan maintains a distinctly bullish view on the eSSD market. Despite some market pessimism that "NAND prices may fall as early as Q4 2026", JPMorgan believes that the continued rise in eSSD penetration will be sufficient to offset weaknesses in the consumer-grade NAND sector. They forecast that the overall eSSD TAM (total addressable market) will exceed 820EB next year, up about 55% year-on-year.

Valuation downgrade: LTA needs to "walk the talk"

The target price cut originates from a re-rating of the valuation multiple.

JPMorgan has reduced the target P/E from approximately 11x (about 0.5 standard deviation above the historical average) to around 9x, returning to the 15-year historical average level for global storage vendors.

The previous premium was given because of expectations that LTA would deliver medium-term earnings stability; but now, JPMorgan thinks that "the market needs to see stable results in the actual numbers before buying in."

The report points out that Kioxia plans to introduce multi-year LTAs as an independent company for the first time from 2027, with the target of reaching 50% LTA coverage by 2028. However, past cases where LTA failed to deliver the expected results have made the market cautious.

JPMorgan clearly states that two key dimensions determine the credibility of LTA: (1) Enforceability, such as the effectiveness of penalty clauses; (2) Its ability to smooth the pricing curve, i.e., whether it can truly reduce price volatility.

"A valuation re-rating will still take time until stable effects are proven in actual results." This is JPMorgan's core view.

Share buybacks: First large-scale buyback in the storage industry

While waiting for LTA validation, Kioxia is sending another signal to the market.

The company announced a share buyback program of up to 800 billion yen as it reported results for Q1 of 2026 (April to June), with the buyback window set from August 3 to October 30.

JPMorgan describes this as the "first large-scale buyback in the storage ecosystem," particularly highlighting the brevity of the buyback window.

In terms of FCF yield, JPMorgan expects FY2026 to FY2028 (based on the share price as of August 7) to be 13%, 27%, and 37%, respectively. The company stated at its June investor day that it will actively return excess free cash flow, primarily via dividends (possibly beginning as soon as the end of FY2026).

JPMorgan currently assumes FCF payout ratios of 10%/30%/50% for FY2026-FY2028, equating to total shareholder return (TSR) of approximately 4%/8%/18%. Should the actual return exceed this assumption, there will be further room for valuation re-rating.

As a reference, both Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix target 50% of accumulated FCF for shareholder returns.

GP series: A medium-term variable for potential supply tightening

JPMorgan also focuses on Kioxia's GP product line—an "ultra-high IOPS" series based on SLC (single-level cell) architecture.

Kioxia's three product line strategies are as follows:

  • CM series (TLC architecture, targeting KV Cache applications)

  • GP series (SLC architecture, targeting HBM supplement/expansion scenarios)

  • LC series (QLC architecture, targeting HDD replacement)

The goal is to increase the eSSD market share from around 10% to 15%.

The GP series aims to achieve 100 million IOPS (input/output operations per second), and the company is planning to sample GP1 (10 million IOPS) to some customers before the end of 2026.

Key supply and demand impact: The "die penalty" (capacity overhead) of SLC architecture is 3 to 4 times that of TLC/QLC. This means that even if the bit contribution from the GP series is limited, its overall consumption of supply is far higher proportionally, and could become a structural factor tightening supply and demand mid-term.

JPMorgan has listed progress in GP series development and customer adoption as important medium-term catalysts.

results.title: 🔥US Stock Macro Outlook – Week of August 10–14, 2026
results.content:
Monday, August 10

  1. Bank of Japan releases Summary of Opinions from its July monetary policy meeting.
  2. Rocket Lab, AST SpaceMobile, and Hims & Hers report after the close (key focus on commercial space and consumer health).
  3. Unitree Technology begins STAR Market subscription (robotics sentiment watch).

Tuesday, August 11

  1. U.S. ADP employment change for the week ending July 25 and July existing home sales.
  2. ★★★★ Super Micro Computer (SMCI), CoreWeave, and Lumentum report after the close — key checks on AI server order conversion, data center ramp/power/financing costs, and 800G/1.6T optical module demand.
  3. Sea and Tencent Music report pre-market; CAVA reports after the close.

Wednesday, August 12

  1. ★★★★★ U.S. July CPI (consensus: headline +3.4% YoY vs. prior 3.5%; core +2.5% YoY vs. prior 2.6%; MoM ~+0.1% headline / ~+0.2% core). Most important macro release of the week after last week’s weak nonfarm; directly impacts September Fed hike pricing (currently ~44% probability).
  2. Tencent Holdings reports (focus on games, advertising, fintech, and AI capex/Hunyuan progress).
  3. ★★★★ Coherent, Cisco, and Nebius report (after-close / some pre-market) — testing AI networking and high-speed optical demand. API/EIA crude inventories plus IEA/OPEC monthly reports also due.

Thursday, August 13

  1. U.S. July PPI and weekly initial jobless claims.
  2. ★★★★★ SanDisk Investor Day (evening Beijing time) — focus on NAND supply/demand, capex, high-bandwidth flash (HBF) roadmap, and long-term margin targets; key for the storage sector.
  3. Google Made by Google event (Pixel 11 series and wearables; deeper Gemini integration).
  4. Fed officials Hammack and Barkin speak.
  5. ★★★★ Applied Materials (AMAT) reports after the close — focus on wafer fab, DRAM, advanced packaging, and semi equipment spending guidance. JD.com.com, SMIC, Hua Hong and other China/semiconductor names also report.

Friday, August 14

  1. ★★★★ U.S. July retail sales, August University of Michigan consumer sentiment preliminary, and 1-year inflation expectations — testing consumer resilience after the cooling labor market.
  2. SEC 13F quarterly holdings disclosure deadline — watch large fund positioning in tech, energy, etc.

Core themes this week center on the July inflation “exam” (CPI following nonfarm, followed by PPI and retail sales to confirm costs and consumption), Fed official signals and the September policy path, plus dense AI infrastructure (CoreWeave, Lumentum, SMCI, Coherent, Cisco, Applied Materials) and storage (SanDisk Investor Day) earnings/events.

 

Note: After last week’s nonfarm surprise of –23k, rate-hike odds have cooled. Softer CPI/core readings plus resilient consumption would support soft-landing trades and growth stocks; hotter data could revive tightening pricing and pressure high-valuation names. Expect elevated volatility — watch data and AI guidance beats/misses closely.

results.title: 🔥 Bitget US Stock Hot Topic Sniping｜2026.08.10 Main Theme: Soft Jobs Data Ignites Rate-Cut Expectations｜AI Software Surge · Chip Rebound · Space Earnings
results.content:
1.Jobs data much weaker than expected, Fed rate-hike odds drop July nonfarm payrolls unexpectedly fell by 23,000 (vs. expected +80,000), with sharp downward revisions to the prior two months and the unemployment rate easing to 4.1%. Markets quickly cut September rate-hike probabilities, Treasury yields fell, and the S&P 500 closed at a record high on Friday, posting its strongest weekly gain since April. 

🎯 Beneficiaries: SPY, QQQ, NVDA; Key catalyst: Soft data reinforces soft-landing + rate-cut expectations, driving capital back into growth stocks.

2. Palantir commercial AI acceleration, U.S. commercial revenue surges PLTR Q2 revenue jumped 93% YoY to roughly $1.94 billion, with U.S. commercial revenue soaring 149% YoY. Total contract value and net retention rate also rose sharply, and full-year guidance was raised again. The stock has surged nearly 40% in the short term as the market re-rates its enterprise AI platform monetization.

🎯 Beneficiaries: PLTR, MSFT; Key catalyst: Enterprise AI orders and raised guidance continue to drive the narrative; watch volume and analyst target upgrades.

3. Chip sector posts strong weekly rebound, NVDA gets SpaceX endorsement NVDA recorded its strongest weekly performance in over a year, with the broader semiconductor sector recovering. On the SpaceX earnings call, Elon Musk stated that future terrestrial and orbital data centers will prioritize NVIDIA chip architectures, reinforcing the AI compute demand story.

🎯 Beneficiaries: NVDA, AMD, MU; Key catalyst: AI infrastructure orders and major-customer endorsements provide support; watch intraday volume and sector linkage.

4. Rocket Lab and AST SpaceMobile report after the close Monday — space theme catalyst RKLB and ASTS are scheduled to report Q2 results after the close on August 10. RKLB recently secured large contracts including from the Space Force, with focus on backlog and launch cadence; ASTS is watched for satellite-to-cellphone commercialization progress. After SpaceX’s elevated AI capex, attention has shifted to mid- and small-cap space names’ execution.

🎯 Beneficiaries: RKLB, ASTS; Key catalyst: Post-close guidance, orders, and launch updates will drive overnight volatility.

5. Progress in Hormuz Strait talks, lower oil supports risk appetite Talks involving the U.S., Iran, and Oman on Strait of Hormuz transit arrangements continue, putting pressure on oil prices. This eases inflation concerns and further supports rate-cut expectations. Risk assets benefit, giving additional liquidity support to tech and growth stocks.

🎯 Beneficiaries: QQQ, XLE (watch inversely); Key catalyst: Geopolitical easing → lower oil/inflation expectations → growth-stock valuation expansion.

Trading note: Soft jobs + AI commercial monetization + chip rebound form a coordinated theme, with capital rotating toward growth and event-driven names. On Monday, focus on space-stock post-close guidance and futures sentiment; manage position size with volume. U.S. stock volatility has intensified recently.
